summary: This is a hangman game implementation in PHP. It picks a random word, then loops asking the player to guess letters one at a time, revealing correct guesses and drawing hangman stages for wrong ones. The game ends when either the player guesses the full word or runs out of incorrect guesses.

explanations.12: array_rand() picks a random index from the words array, so we get a random word each time.
explanations.26: PHP_EOL is a constant that prints a newline character in a way that works on any operating system.
explanations.33: str_split() breaks the word into individual letters so we can check each one separately.
explanations.40: trim() removes the extra spaces we added after the last letter.
explanations.54: fgets(STDIN) reads a line of text that the player types into the terminal.
explanations.56: strlen() counts characters (should be exactly 1), and ctype_alpha() checks that it's a letter.
explanations.61: strtolower() converts the guess to lowercase so 'A' and 'a' are treated the same.
explanations.70: strpos() returns false if the guessed letter is not found anywhere in the word.
explanations.74: This line has a bug — it calls displayWord() which outputs text, making it impossible to check if the word is fully guessed. It should compare the revealed letters differently.
explanations.80: This checks if we've lost by running out of guesses (incorrectGuesses reaches 0).
